title: 면접을 망친 친구에게: 위로하고 조언하기
objective: Say why something went wrong with -는 통에 and suggest what to do next with -는 게 어때요?
summary: Learn how to comfort a friend after a bad day and give gentle advice.
setting: A café after work. 소라 had a job interview yesterday and looks upset. Her friend 지훈 listens, comforts her, and gives some advice.

task.title: Comfort, advise, and explain
task.line: Use the dialogue and the expressions on page 1 to fill in, choose, or answer in Korean.

words.meaning: because of (a busy or annoying situation); used only when the result is bad. Use the present form (-는) even for past events.
words.example: 아이가 밤새 우는 통에 한숨도 못 잤어요.
words.exampleMeaning: The baby cried all night, so I didn't get a wink of sleep.

words.meaning: to be upset, to feel hurt or frustrated
words.exampleMeaning: I'm upset because I lost my favorite umbrella.

words.example: 동생은 시험에 떨어진 뒤로 계속 자책하고 있어요.
words.exampleMeaning: My younger sibling has been blaming himself ever since he failed the exam.

words.meaning: why don't you...? (a soft way to give advice)
words.example: 혼자 고민하지 말고 선생님께 물어보는 게 어때요?
words.exampleMeaning: Instead of worrying alone, why don't you ask your teacher?
Let's eat first and talk after.

dialogue.korean: 소라 씨, 얼굴이 안 좋아 보여요. 무슨 일 있어요?
dialogue.meaning: Sora, you don't look well. Is something wrong?

dialogue.korean: 어제 면접을 봤는데 망친 것 같아요. 아침에 지하철이 멈추는 통에 10분이나 늦었거든요.
dialogue.meaning: I had an interview yesterday, and I think I blew it. The subway stopped in the morning, so I was a whole 10 minutes late.

dialogue.korean: 아이고, 정말 속상했겠어요. 그건 소라 씨 잘못이 아니잖아요.
dialogue.meaning: Oh no, you must have been so upset. That wasn't your fault.

dialogue.korean: 결과는 기다려 봐야 알죠. 그동안 다른 회사에도 계속 지원해 보는 게 어때요?
dialogue.meaning: You won't know the result until it comes out. In the meantime, why don't you keep applying to other companies?

dialogue.korean: 그게 좋겠어요. 일단 오늘은 푹 쉬고 내일부터 다시 해 볼게요.
dialogue.meaning: That sounds good. For now, I'll get some good rest today and start again tomorrow.

exercises: Fill in the blanks with -는 통에 and the verb in brackets: ① 윗집에서 공사를 ____ (하다) 공부에 집중이 안 돼요. ② 버스가 갑자기 ____ (서다) 넘어질 뻔했어요.
Choose the sentence where -는 통에 is NOT natural: (a) 비가 오는 통에 소풍이 취소됐어요. (b) 친구가 도와주는 통에 숙제가 빨리 끝났어요. (c) 길이 막히는 통에 약속에 늦었어요.
Your friend says, "발표를 망쳐서 너무 속상해." Choose the best comforting reply: (a) 그러니까 미리 준비했어야지. (b) 나도 발표 잘하는 방법은 몰라. (c) 그럴 때도 있어. 너무 자책하지 마.
Give advice. Fill in the blank with -는 게 어때요?: A: 요즘 밤에 잠이 잘 안 와요. B: 자기 전에 휴대폰을 ____ (안 보다)?
Read the dialogue and answer in Korean with -는 통에: 소라 씨는 왜 면접에 늦었어요?
answers: ① 하는 통에 ② 서는 통에
(b) — -는 통에 is used only when the result is bad.
지하철이 멈추는 통에 늦었어요. (아침에 지하철이 멈추는 통에 10분 늦었어요.)
